summary: The prepared base already fixed GLM-5.2 correction-bias preservation at allocation and the aiter top-k boundary. The remaining aiter router GEMM output-dtype defect reproduced on gfx950 and was corrected by requesting torch.float32 output; a two-shape GPU regression now passes.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the change, actual aiter_dsv3_router_gemm calls returned torch.bfloat16 for (8,7168,256) and (65,512,64) on gfx950; maximum absolute errors versus independent fp32 torch linear references were 0.0238833427 and 0.0124273300.
The production router dimensions and an independent fallback shape both return finite fp32 tensors with the expected dimensions on the assigned gfx950 GPU (1 test, 2 subtests).
The existing correction-bias allocation, architecture-boundary, bf16-collapse, and routing-divergence regression coverage passes (9 tests).
After the change both shapes return torch.float32, but the installed untuned aiter fallback retains bf16-level internal rounding versus an independent fp32 torch linear reference.
No whitespace errors in the delivered changes.

gpu_execution.evidence: Single AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015; raw logs in reports/j-10fb71b436d3/raw/gpu_before.txt, gpu_after_pytest_final.txt, and gpu_after_numeric.txt.

remaining_limitations: No GLM-5.2 weights were available, so no full-model semantic or accuracy reproduction was performed.
Only one assigned gfx950 GPU was used; no multi-GPU or multi-node behavior was evaluated.

The installed aiter dispatcher had no tuned entry for the tested shapes. Although the corrected API returns fp32, its fallback showed bf16-level internal rounding, so improved numerical accuracy inside aiter is not claimed.
No native SGLang or aiter source was changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
